The two arcs are A→B and B→A, both with sweep-flag 0. Reversing direction with the same sweep flag places the second semicircle on the opposite side of the chord, so the two semicircles together form a full circle centered at the chord's midpoint, (63.88, 44.22). This is the standard SVG idiom for drawing a circle with two arcs. The program's distinct centers come from treating the exact-180° arcs as ambiguous; they do not indicate a non-circular outline.

Other options are ruled out: rx = ry rules out an ellipse, there are no radii to a center so it is not a sector, and there are no straight segments so it is not a polygon.
